method.topology: PC sender to Ubuntu receiver over physical LAN. CD uses a local Worker through reverse SSH only for rendezvous/fallback; CD actual transport telemetry is recorded; default strict mode requires TCP direct bytes. --require-tcp0 permits annotated fallback diagnostics. croc uses a private TCP relay on the receiver machine with --no-local. Both carry bulk bytes over the LAN once; their rendezvous topology differs.
method.timing: Receiver duration starts before SSH receiver launch, ends after receiver process exits. Durable duration also includes remote file and output-directory fsync before SSH exits. Readiness and total measured separately. SHA256 verification runs over a separate SSH command outside all transfer timings.
method.limitations: Three trials by default, one physical LAN, no WAN/browser/concurrency claim. Both tools use identical staged binaries at both ends. croc default and no-compress both measured. Remote infrastructure uses disk, local Worker SQLite uses RAM. SSH launch overhead is present in each receiver duration.
method.durability: Native receiver exit observed by remote launcher; file/directory fsync added equally for both tools. Existing internal fsync differences remain included.
